acceptance.given: Aggregate evaluation receives the complete required Matrix Case/input/subject execution set with one required execution intentionally absent.

oracle.expected: The aggregate evaluation reports failure and identifies the missing required execution; it never returns success for the incomplete set.
forbidden: The aggregate reports success while any required Matrix Case, input, or subject execution is missing.
oracle.observable: Executed aggregate result and its missing-execution diagnostic are captured from the matrix evaluation invocation.

acceptance.then: Execute the aggregate check after removing one required execution from an otherwise complete Matrix Case set.
acceptance.when: Any required Matrix Case execution is missing.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The aggregate accepts an incomplete Matrix Case execution set or omits the missing-execution failure.

slice_hint.behavior_change: Ensure aggregate evaluation fails closed whenever any required Matrix Case, input, or subject execution is absent.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: Preserve existing aggregate result schema and failure semantics; rollback only the missing-execution guard and its test.

slice_hint.state_transition: complete execution set -> one required execution missing -> aggregate failure with diagnostic
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: The aggregate result is non-success and explicitly reports the absent required execution.

acceptance.given: The existing test_candidate_identity fixture is available while the relevant verification is assembled and executed.

oracle.expected: The fixture remains used only for its declared verification role, and behavior is established by executed assertions rather than by checking that the file exists.
forbidden: The fixture is removed from its declared role.
Fixture existence alone is treated as behavior proof.
oracle.observable: The executed verification records assertion outcomes and separately records fixture-role usage; no existence-only pass is accepted.

acceptance.then: Run the candidate-identity verification and inspect its assertion-backed result.
acceptance.when: When assembling and executing the relevant verification.

failure_intents.selector_intent: The verification passes solely because test_candidate_identity.py exists or the fixture is used outside its declared role.

affected_subjects: test_candidate_identity fixture role and behavior-proof separation
slice_hint.behavior_change: Keep test_candidate_identity.py confined to its declared fixture role and require executed assertions for behavior proof.

rollback_scope.state_or_schema_compatibility: No schema or state change; rollback only role/proof enforcement.

slice_hint.state_transition: fixture present -> role-bound execution -> assertion-backed behavior result
slice_hint.terminal_predicate: Verification succeeds only when declared-role usage and executed assertions are both observed.
